newsitem.title: SPAIN: Catalans say Spain should study taxing insurance.
newsitem.headline: Catalans say Spain should study taxing insurance.

text.p: The Spanish government should study imposing a tax on private insurance to allow it to meet its budget deficit targets, a spokesman for its Catalan nationalist allies in parliament said on Tuesday.
Joaquim Molins, spokesman for the Convergence and Unity (CiU) coalition, told radio station SER that a tax on private insurance on cars and homes "must be studied".
"(The government) has not taken any decisions on the budget yet," he said.
The conservative government of Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar is currently in talks with CiU to secure its support for the 1997 budget which must be presented to parliament by the end of the month.
Molins said Spain needed to harmonise with the rest of the European Union and it was good to bring taxes on certain goods in line with other countries.
